executionScopes.title: Fix join-meeting stuck-on-joining bug and build end-to-end Test-event validation harness
executionScopes.description:
## Why this exists

Two interlocked problems:

1. **Bug**: Clicking "Join" on any meeting transitions session state to "joining" and stays there forever. No information surfaces in any log. The full join -> transcribe -> decide -> speak pipeline cannot be validated until this is fixed.

2. **No end-to-end validation**: We have no harness that exercises the real stack against a real Google Meet. Unit tests pass while the user-visible journey is broken. We need a reproducible test program that drives the full stack end-to-end.

These must be solved together: the harness is how we prove the bug is fixed and stays fixed.

## Setup (testing environment)

- Johnny (bot identity): nikita.rabykin@aikamatkat.fi
- User (running tests, listening): nikita.rabykin@gmail.com
- Test calendar event: exactly one Google Calendar event titled "Test", owned by the user account. The harness owns this event — it may rearrange, retitle, reschedule, or otherwise mutate it freely between runs.

## What this delivers

### Part A: Diagnose and fix the join-stuck bug

- Add structured logging at every stage of the join path: scheduler dispatch, worker container spawn, Playwright navigation, Google sign-in, "Join now" click, bot_sessions.status transitions, audio bridge attach
- Logs must include session_id and surface both in 'docker compose logs' and 'bot_sessions.logs'
- UI session view must surface the most recent failure stage when join fails — no silent perpetual "joining"
- Identify and fix the actual root cause (candidates: missing Chromium flags, Xvfb not started, account cookies missing, Meet "Ask to join" gate, container spawn failure, race between scheduler and worker)

### Part B: End-to-end validation harness

Single command ('uv run python -m johnny.e2e --mode=<mode>' or 'make e2e MODE=<mode>') that:
  1. Ensures the "Test" event exists, owned by user account, with both bot and user invited, Meet link attached
  2. Reschedules the Test event to start within ~1 minute (so each run kicks off quickly without waiting for the original schedule)
  3. Creates a meeting_config for the Test event with the chosen mode
  4. Waits for scheduler to spawn the meet-worker container (or invokes the same code path directly)
  5. Verifies the bot joins (Meet participant list includes Johnny, bot_sessions.status flips to "joined")
  6. Injects a known audio sample into the meeting (second Playwright participant playing fixture audio, or synthetic injector piping audio into the room)
  7. Verifies transcripts persisted to transcript_chunks with expected content
  8. Verifies router decisions persisted to agent_decisions
  9. In Limited auto-speak mode, verifies an utterance is persisted to agent_utterances
  10. Tears down: bot leaves meeting, worker container stops, Test event reset for next run

- Selectable mode: listen / suggest / approval / auto_speak_limited — every mode must pass independently
- PASS/FAIL output per phase with diagnostic logs (same format as Johnny-f7k smoke test)
- Exit code 0 only when every phase passes

### Part C: Documentation

- "Running end-to-end" section in docs/SETUP_LOCAL.md linking to the harness
- Document the Test-event convention (one event named "Test", both identities invited, freely mutable)
- Document how to swap modes and what each verifies

## Parent relationship

This issue sits ABOVE Johnny-kgc — Johnny-kgc becomes its child. Rationale: this is the meta-validation gate proving the entire epic actually works end-to-end against real infrastructure. Johnny-kgc delivers features; this issue validates them.

## Out of scope

- Multi-tenant fixtures (single user, single Test event only)
- Load / concurrent meeting tests
- Replacing unit tests (this is additive)
- CI integration (follow-up)
